boundary: BIT describes Aion publicly as an agentic research platform its investment team uses daily. Its internals are not public. These surfaces are inferred from BIT's public AI Engineer and Data Platform roles and its product descriptions. They are a map for judging where a development would land, never a claim about BIT's private architecture.

surfaces.name: Data platform
surfaces.what: Pipelines that ingest filings, transcripts, market and alternative data, and keep it queryable and clean.
surfaces.scope: Ingestion adapters, scheduling and orchestration, lakehouse or warehouse storage, schema and data-quality checks, lineage, and the SQL and Python layer analysts and agents query.

surfaces.name: Retrieval
surfaces.what: Finding the right evidence in the research corpus — search, embeddings, ranking, filters.
surfaces.scope: Chunking, embedding models, vector and keyword search, reranking, metadata filters by company, date and source type, and how much retrieval is needed given model context limits.

surfaces.name: Extraction
surfaces.what: Turning documents and text into structured, attributed fields an analyst can trace back to a source.
surfaces.scope: Prompt and schema design, structured output and function calling, document and table parsing, source spans and citation fidelity, and silent extraction error.

surfaces.name: Agents
surfaces.what: Research skills that plan, use tools, run code and draft — the part BIT names publicly as Aion.
surfaces.scope: Planning and multi-step execution, tool use, memory, reusable research skills, code sidecars, agent harnesses and protocols, and long-horizon reliability.

surfaces.name: Models and cost
surfaces.what: Which model runs which task, with fallbacks, caching, and the token and dollar cost of each workflow.
surfaces.scope: Model and reasoning-effort selection per task, price-performance changes, prompt caching and batching, context limits, fallbacks and version pinning, provider availability and deprecation.

surfaces.name: Evaluation
surfaces.what: Knowing whether output is right — accuracy, hallucination, uncertainty, and regressions when something changes.
surfaces.scope: Eval design and datasets, LLM-as-judge methods, hallucination and calibration measurement, human-in-the-loop review, regression testing across prompt and model changes, and benchmark transferability.

surfaces.name: Operations
surfaces.what: Running it safely in production — what an agent may touch, plus tracing, monitoring and failure recovery.
surfaces.scope: Permissions and entitlements over sensitive or licensed data, scoped tool access and sandboxing for agents, audit trails, tracing across multi-step runs, latency and error monitoring, and incident recovery for scheduled jobs.
